summary: At 21 people per square mile, Glenn County is one of the emptiest inhabited stretches of California's Sacramento Valley — a place where the dominant visual experience is an unbroken horizon of rice paddies, almond orchards, and irrigated pasture stretching toward the Coast Ranges to the west and the Sierra Nevada foothills distantly to the east. Agriculture isn't just the backdrop here; it *is* the economy, with rice milling, almond processing, and cattle operations forming the employment spine, supplemented by county government and a small healthcare sector clustered around the towns of Willows and Orland. That agricultural orientation helps explain the affordability math: a median home value of $338,400 against a median household income of roughly $70,500 produces a price-to-income ratio under 5:1, strikingly low for California, while median rent at $1,103 per month stays well below what most of the state demands. The tradeoff is isolation — Interstate 5 runs through the county but connects you to Chico (the nearest college town with broader retail and medical services) about 30 minutes east, and Sacramento sits roughly 90 minutes south. With 9.4 hours of daily sunshine and summer highs that regularly push into the mid-90s, the climate rewards early mornings and late evenings spent along the Sacramento River or at the Sacramento National Wildlife Refuge on the county's southern edge. Glenn County is, fundamentally, a place where affordable land and vast sky come bundled with the requirement that you build much of your own daily infrastructure — entertainment, career mobility, and variety don't arrive by default.
